events.title: Neolithic Settlement
events.description: Earliest agricultural settlements appear in Turkmenistan region, particularly in southern foothills of Kopet Dag mountains. Archaeological evidence shows local inhabitants began cultivating wheat and barley, domesticating goats and sheep. These early settlements laid foundation for later civilizational development.

events.title: Altyn-Depe Culture
events.description: Altyn-Depe becomes important Bronze Age city in Central Asia, located near present-day Ashgabat. This city featured complex irrigation systems, craft workshops and trade networks, maintaining commercial relations with Mesopotamian and Indus Valley civilizations. Archaeological discoveries include fine pottery, bronze artifacts and seals.

events.title: Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex
events.description: Southern Turkmenistan becomes important component of Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex (BMAC). This civilization known for distinctive architectural style, exquisite gold and silver vessels, and complex religious rituals. Margiana Oasis becomes important agricultural and trade center.

events.title: Indo-European Migration
events.description: Indo-European tribes begin migrating into Turkmenistan region, bringing new languages, cultures and technologies. These migrations profoundly impact local population structure and cultural development, laying foundation for later Persian cultural spread.

events.title: Early Iron Age
events.description: Turkmenistan enters Iron Age, with iron tools and weapons becoming widespread. This technological advancement promotes increased agricultural productivity and enhanced military capabilities. Meanwhile, nomadic culture begins emerging in steppe regions, forming interactions with settled agricultural civilization.

events.title: Scythian Activity
events.description: Scythian nomadic peoples actively present in northern Turkmenistan steppe regions. They are renowned for superb horsemanship and metalworking crafts. Scythian culture profoundly influences regional nomadic traditions.

events.title: Achaemenid Persian Conquest
events.description: Cyrus the Great incorporates Turkmenistan region into Achaemenid Persian Empire. Region divided into satrapies of Parthia and Margiana. Persian rule brings Zoroastrianism, Persian language and script, and advanced administrative systems.

events.title: Greco-Persian Wars Impact
events.description: During Persian Empire's wars with Greek city-states, Turkmenistan as part of Persian Empire provides troops and resources. Regional cavalry plays important role in Persian forces. Wars promote East-West cultural exchange.

events.title: Alexander the Great's Conquest
events.description: Alexander the Great conquers Turkmenistan, establishing Alexandria in Margiana (near present-day Merv). Hellenistic culture begins merging with local cultures, producing unique Greco-Bactrian civilization. This period witnesses flourishing of art, architecture and science.

events.title: Rise of Parthian Empire
events.description: Parthians under Arsaces I establish Parthian Empire, with Turkmenistan becoming core territory. Parthian Empire becomes important intermediary for Silk Road trade between Rome and China, controlling East-West trade routes. Nisa becomes important Parthian royal city and burial site.

events.title: Sassanid Dynasty Rule
events.description: Sassanid Dynasty overthrows Parthian Empire, Turkmenistan again becomes part of Persian Empire. Under Sassanid rule, Zoroastrianism further develops, Persian culture and art reach new heights. Architectural and artistic works from this period still visible in places like Merv.

events.title: Hephthalite Invasion
events.description: Hephthalites (White Huns) move south from Central Asian steppes, posing serious threat to Sassanid Persia. Turkmenistan becomes frontline region contested by both sides. Warfare during this period damages local economy and culture but also promotes exchange and fusion of different peoples.

events.title: Turkic Khaganate Influence
events.description: Turkic Khaganate rises in Central Asia, extending its sphere of influence to northern Turkmenistan. This marks first major impact of Turkic peoples on region, laying foundation for later Turkification. Turkic peoples bring new nomadic culture and military technology.

events.title: Sassanid-Byzantine Wars Impact
events.description: Prolonged wars between Sassanid Persia and Byzantine Empire affect Turkmenistan. Region must provide substantial troops and resources for war effort, causing increased economic burden. Wars weaken Sassanid Dynasty's strength, creating conditions for later Arab conquest.

events.title: Arab Conquest and Islamization
events.description: Arab Muslim armies conquer Turkmenistan, beginning region's Islamization process. Merv becomes important Islamic learning center, attracting scholars from various regions. Local inhabitants gradually convert to Islam, Arabic becomes religious and academic language.

events.title: Abbasid Caliphate Rule
events.description: Abbasid Caliphate replaces Umayyad Dynasty, Turkmenistan becomes eastern frontier of Abbasid Caliphate. Merv develops as important administrative and cultural center, called 'Mother of the World.' This period witnesses Islamic civilization's golden age, with science, philosophy and literature flourishing.

events.title: Tahirid Dynasty Autonomy
events.description: Tahirid Dynasty establishes semi-independent rule in Khorasan, with Turkmenistan becoming part of their territory. This marks decline of Abbasid central power and rise of local dynasties. Tahirid rulers promote Persian cultural revival and local autonomy development.

events.title: Saffarid Dynasty Rule
events.description: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth establishes Saffarid Dynasty, controlling vast territories including Turkmenistan. Saffarid Dynasty known for military strength and challenge to Abbasid Caliphate. This period witnesses rise of local military nobility.

events.title: Samanid Dynasty Rule
events.description: Samanid Dynasty establishes rule over Turkmenistan, promoting Persian cultural and linguistic revival. Samanid rulers patronize literature and science, producing many important Persian poets and scholars. Bukhara and Samarkand become important cultural centers.

events.title: Seljuk Turkic Conquest
events.description: Seljuk Turks under Tughril Beg conquer Turkmenistan, establishing Seljuk Empire. This marks rise of Turkic peoples on Central Asian political stage. Seljuks adopt Islam and Persian administrative traditions while maintaining Turkic military culture.

events.title: Khwarazmshah Rule
events.description: Khwarazmshah Dynasty establishes rule over Turkmenistan. Anushtegin Gharchai and successors develop Khwarazm into powerful independent kingdom. This period witnesses trade prosperity and cultural development.

events.title: Mongol Conquest
events.description: Mongol armies under Genghis Khan conquer Turkmenistan, destroying Khwarazm Kingdom. Important cities like Merv completely destroyed, massive populations killed or enslaved. This conquest has catastrophic impact on region's population and culture, many cities never recover.

events.title: Mongol Empire Rule
events.description: Turkmenistan becomes part of Chagatai Khanate of Mongol Empire. Mongol rulers implement military control but allow local autonomy to some degree. Silk Road trade partially recovers during Pax Mongolica, but region's urban civilization suffers irreversible damage. Many settled farmers shift to nomadic lifestyle.

events.title: Ilkhanate Rule
events.description: After Hulagu establishes Ilkhanate, Turkmenistan becomes part of its territory. Ilkhanate ruler Ghazan Khan converts to Islam, promoting Islamization of region. This period sees Mongol-Persian cultural fusion, with Persian language restored as administrative language while Mongol military traditions preserved.

events.title: Timurid Conquest
events.description: Timur (Tamerlane) conquers Turkmenistan, incorporating it into Timurid Empire. Though Timur's rule brutal, it also promotes artistic and architectural development. Samarkand becomes empire's glorious capital, attracting craftsmen and scholars from various regions.

events.title: Timurid Dynasty Period
events.description: After Timur's death, his descendants continue ruling Turkmenistan. Rulers like Ulugh Beg patronize science and arts, making Samarkand and Herat important cultural centers. This period witnesses golden age of Persian-Turkic culture, producing many outstanding poets, scholars and artists. However, internal conflicts among Timur's descendants gradually weaken dynasty's power.

events.title: Uzbek Khanate Rule
events.description: Uzbeks under Shaybani Khan conquer Turkmenistan, establishing rule of Bukhara and Khiva Khanates. This period witnesses further fusion of Turkic-Mongol culture with Islamic civilization. Turkmen tribes begin forming modern tribal structures.

events.title: Formation of Turkmen Tribal Confederations
events.description: Major tribal confederations of modern Turkmen nation form during this period, including Teke, Yomud, Saryk, Ersary and Choudur tribes. These tribes develop unique nomadic culture, famous for horse breeding, carpet weaving and warrior traditions. Inter-tribal competition and alliance relationships shape Turkmen social structure.

events.title: Nadir Shah's Conquest
events.description: Nadir Shah of Persia conquers Turkmenistan, attempting to rebuild Persian Empire's glory. Though Nadir Shah's rule brief, it significantly impacts region's political landscape. After his death, region again falls into fragmentation.

events.title: Khanate Division and Tribal Conflicts
events.description: Turkmenistan divided between Khiva Khanate, Bukhara Emirate and Persia. Turkmen tribes maintain relative independence, frequently conflicting with these powers. Inter-tribal raids and slave trade characterize this period. Russia begins showing interest in region.

events.title: Beginning of the Great Game
events.description: Russian Empire and British Empire engage in intense geopolitical competition in Central Asia, known as 'The Great Game.' Turkmenistan becomes focus of rivalry between two great empires due to its strategic location. During this period, Russia begins systematically collecting intelligence on Turkmen tribes, preparing for later military conquest.

events.title: Treaty of Gulistan
events.description: Russia and Persia sign Treaty of Gulistan, with Persia ceding Caucasus region to Russia. This brings Russian power closer to Turkmenistan, laying foundation for future expansion. Treaty changes regional power balance.

events.title: Treaty of Turkmenchay
events.description: Russia and Persia sign Treaty of Turkmenchay, further weakening Persian influence in region. Russia gains navigation rights in Caspian Sea, facilitating later expansion toward Turkmenistan. Treaty makes Russia dominant power in Caspian region.

events.title: Internal Turmoil in Khiva Khanate
events.description: Khiva Khanate weakened by internal power struggles, unable to effectively control Turkmen tribes. Turkmen tribes use this opportunity to strengthen autonomy, but region also falls into chaos. This political vacuum provides opportunity for Russian intervention.

events.title: Russian Establishment of Krasnovodsk
events.description: Russia establishes Krasnovodsk fortress (present-day Turkmenbashi) on eastern Caspian shore, marking beginning of Russian conquest of Turkmenistan. This port becomes main base for Russian military entry into Turkmenistan and later starting point of Trans-Caspian Railway.

events.title: Khiva Expedition
events.description: Russia launches large-scale military expedition against Khiva Khanate, forcing it to become protectorate. This expedition weakens Khiva's influence over Turkmen tribes, allowing Russia to directly confront Turkmen tribes. Many Turkmen tribes begin recognizing seriousness of Russian threat.

events.title: First Geok-Tepe Expedition
events.description: Russian forces attempt first assault on Teke tribe's Geok-Tepe fortress but suffer devastating defeat. Turkmen warriors demonstrate tenacious resistance spirit, inflicting heavy casualties on Russian forces. This failure makes Russia realize need for more adequate preparation to conquer Turkmen tribes.

events.title: Battle of Geok-Tepe
events.description: Russian forces engage in fierce battle with Teke tribe at Geok-Tepe fortress. Despite brave Turkmen warrior resistance, they ultimately defeated by Russian modern weapons. About 15,000 Turkmens die in this battle, marking end of Teke tribal resistance.

events.title: Completion of Russian Conquest
events.description: Russian forces under General Skobelev completely conquer Turkmenistan, establishing Trans-Caspian Province. Turkmen tribal independence era ends, region incorporated into Russian Empire. Russia begins implementing colonial policies, building railways, developing cotton cultivation.

events.title: Yomud Tribal Resistance
events.description: Yomud Turkmen tribes continue resisting Russian rule, launching multiple uprisings. Russian forces employ brutal suppression tactics, destroying tribal camps and confiscating livestock. Many Yomuds flee to Persia and Afghanistan seeking refuge. These resistances ultimately crushed, marking submission of all major Turkmen tribes to Russian rule.

events.title: Trans-Caspian Railway Construction
events.description: Russia begins constructing Trans-Caspian Railway from Krasnovodsk to Samarkand, completed in 1888. This railway completely transforms Turkmenistan's economic and social structure, promoting Russian immigration and modernization process.

events.title: Consolidation of Russian Colonial Rule
events.description: Russia establishes complete colonial administrative system in Turkmenistan, promoting Russian language education and legal system. Large numbers of Russian and other Slavic immigrants flood in, changing regional demographic structure. Meanwhile, Russia begins systematically developing local cotton cultivation, making Turkmenistan important cotton producer for Russia.

events.title: Foundation of Ashgabat City
events.description: Ashgabat officially becomes administrative center of Trans-Caspian Province. Under Russian rule, this city develops rapidly, becoming important political, economic and cultural center. Russian architecture and urban planning begin transforming Turkmenistan's urban landscape.

events.title: Constitutional Movement Impact
events.description: Impact of Russia's 1905 Revolution and Constitutional Movement reaches Turkmenistan. Some intellectuals and workers begin demanding reforms, though on limited scale, marking emergence of modern political consciousness. This also represents first organized political activity in Turkmenistan.

events.title: Central Asian Uprising
events.description: Turkmens participate in great Central Asian uprising against Russian rule, protesting forced conscription and colonial policies. Though uprising suppressed, it demonstrates local people's dissatisfaction with Russian rule. This uprising plants seeds for later revolutionary movements.

events.title: Russian Revolution Impact
events.description: After Russian October Revolution, Turkmenistan falls into chaos. Bolsheviks, White Army, British intervention forces and local nationalists engage in complex struggle. This period called 'Turkmenistan Civil War,' lasting several years.

events.title: Transcaspian Provisional Government
events.description: Ashgabat establishes anti-Bolshevik Transcaspian Provisional Government, supported by Britain. This government attempts to maintain regional independence but faces internal and external pressures. This period marks brief attempt at Turkmen political autonomy.

events.title: British Intervention Withdrawal
events.description: British forces withdraw from Turkmenistan, ending brief occupation of region. This creates conditions for return of Bolshevik forces. British withdrawal reflects decline of British influence in Central Asia after World War I.

events.title: Red Army Control of Turkmenistan
events.description: Soviet Red Army completely controls Turkmenistan region, overthrowing anti-Bolshevik regimes throughout area. Bolsheviks begin establishing Soviet power in region but face serious resistance, particularly from conservative religious forces and tribal leaders.

events.title: Basmachi Movement
events.description: Turkmen tribes and religious leaders launch Basmachi rebellion against Soviet rule. This armed resistance movement continues for years, with Soviet forces deploying substantial military force for suppression. Basmachi movement reflects traditional society's strong backlash against communist reforms.

events.title: Establishment of Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic
events.description: Soviet government establishes Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic, becoming USSR constituent republic. This marks establishment of Turkmenistan's modern state borders. Soviet regime begins implementing radical social and economic reforms.

events.title: Script Reform
events.description: Soviet government changes Turkmen language script from Arabic to Latin script, then to Cyrillic in 1940. These reforms aim to sever connections with Islamic traditions and promote Soviet culture spread.

events.title: Collectivization and Great Purge
events.description: Stalin's collectivization policy forces Turkmen nomads to settle, destroying traditional tribal structures. During Great Purge, many Turkmen intellectuals and religious leaders executed or exiled. This period severely impacts Turkmen traditional culture.

events.title: Great Terror Period
events.description: Stalin's Great Purge reached its peak in Turkmenistan. Nearly entire Turkmen Communist Party leadership was purged, thousands of intellectuals, officials and religious figures accused as 'enemies of the people' and executed or exiled to Gulag. This terror campaign destroyed Turkmen elite class, causing profound social trauma.

events.title: World War II
events.description: Turkmenistan participated in anti-fascist war as part of Soviet Union. About 300,000 Turkmens were conscripted, with approximately half perishing in war. During war, many factories evacuated from west to Turkmenistan, promoting industrialization. Turkmen oil and natural gas resources made important contributions to Soviet war effort.

events.title: Great Ashgabat Earthquake
events.description: Magnitude 7.3 earthquake destroys Ashgabat, killing approximately 110,000 people. This is one of 20th century's most severe earthquake disasters. Soviet government rebuilds city, but earthquake's impact lasts decades.

events.title: Soviet Modernization
events.description: Turkmenistan achieves rapid modernization under Soviet rule. Large irrigation projects, industrial facilities and educational institutions built. Natural gas industry begins developing, becoming important energy supplier for USSR. Meanwhile, Russian education spreads, urbanization accelerates.

events.title: Gorbachev Reforms
events.description: Gorbachev's glasnost and perestroika policies have limited impact in Turkmenistan. Saparmurat Niyazov becomes First Secretary of Turkmen Communist Party, beginning to consolidate personal power. Compared to other Soviet republics, political changes in Turkmenistan relatively slow.

events.title: Sovereignty Declaration
events.description: Turkmenistan Supreme Soviet passes sovereignty declaration, declaring republic laws superior to union laws. This important step toward independence, though Niyazov initially not eager to leave USSR.

events.title: Turkmenistan Independence
events.description: Against backdrop of USSR dissolution, Turkmenistan declares independence. Saparmurat Niyazov becomes first president. Independence referendum passes with 94% support. Turkmenistan becomes one of world's youngest independent nations.

events.title: New Constitution and Neutrality Policy
events.description: Turkmenistan adopts new constitution, establishing presidential system. Niyazov declares permanent neutrality policy, not joining any military alliances. This policy later recognized by UN, becoming cornerstone of Turkmenistan's foreign policy.

events.title: Beginning of Personality Cult
events.description: Niyazov begins establishing personality cult, calling himself 'Turkmenbashi' (Father of Turkmens). His portraits and statues appear throughout country, personality cult reaches extreme levels. This period begins Turkmenistan's unique authoritarian rule model.

events.title: President for Life
events.description: Turkmenistan parliament declares Niyazov president for life. This marks complete halt of democratic process and establishment of personal dictatorship. Opposition suppressed, media under strict control.

events.title: Renaming of Months and Days
events.description: Niyazov ordered renaming of months and days of week after Turkmen historical figures and concepts from Ruhnama. January renamed 'Turkmenbashi', April after his mother's name. This extreme personality cult measure attracted international attention and criticism, becoming symbol of absurdity of Niyazov's rule.

events.title: Publication of Ruhnama
events.description: Niyazov publishes 'Ruhnama' (Book of Soul), claiming it as spiritual guide for Turkmen people. This book becomes mandatory study material, even placed alongside Quran in mosques. This reflects Niyazov's attempt to create new ideological system.

events.title: Natural Gas Export Agreements
events.description: Turkmenistan signs natural gas export agreements with multiple countries, beginning large-scale natural gas resource development. Gas revenues become main source of state finances, but also intensify dependence on single resource.

events.title: Assassination Attempt
events.description: Niyazov survives assassination attempt, government accuses former Foreign Minister Boris Shikhmuradov of plotting. Large-scale purge follows, hundreds arrested. This incident further strengthens political repression.

events.title: Niyazov's Death
events.description: Saparmurat Niyazov suddenly dies, ending 15 years of dictatorial rule. His death triggers power struggle, ultimately Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov gains power.

events.title: Berdimuhamedov Elected President
events.description: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov wins presidential election, beginning new rule period. He promises reforms, but basic authoritarian structure remains unchanged. Some extreme policies from Niyazov era cancelled.

events.title: Constitutional Amendment
events.description: New constitution abolishes presidential life tenure, limiting term to 7 years. Simultaneously expands presidential powers, establishes People's Council as supreme authority. These reforms viewed as limited political opening.

events.title: Turkmenistan-China Gas Pipeline
events.description: Turkmenistan-China gas pipeline opens, marking important progress in energy export diversification. This pipeline reduces dependence on Russia, strengthens economic relations with China.

events.title: Berdimuhamedov Re-election
events.description: Berdimuhamedov re-elected in presidential election with 97% vote share. Election criticized by international observers as unfree and unfair. Political opposition continues facing suppression.

events.title: Third Re-election and Personality Cult
events.description: Berdimuhamedov elected president for third time. His personality cult reaches new heights, called 'Arkadag' (Protector). Golden tooth statue and various bizarre personality cult forms become international attention focus.

events.title: Door to Hell Closure Attempt
events.description: Government announces plan to close Darvaza gas crater (called 'Door to Hell') burning for nearly 50 years, to protect environment and gas resources. This decision attracts international attention as site has become famous tourist attraction.

events.title: COVID-19 Denial Policy
events.description: Turkmenistan becomes one of few countries claiming no COVID-19 cases. Government bans use of word 'coronavirus,' adopting extreme denial policy. This stance questioned by international community.

events.title: Power Transition
events.description: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov announces resignation from presidency, his son Serdar Berdimuhamedov elected new president in special election. This marks Turkmenistan's first father-son power transition, establishing de facto hereditary system.

events.title: Beginning of Serdar Era
events.description: 40-year-old Serdar Berdimuhamedov becomes one of world's youngest presidents. He promises advancing digitalization and modernization, but fundamental nature of political system remains unchanged. Father Gurbanguly continues as People's Council Chairman, maintaining important influence.

events.title: Economic Challenges and Reform Attempts
events.description: Turkmenistan faces serious economic difficulties, including currency devaluation, food shortages and declining energy export revenues. New government announces series of economic reform measures, including attracting foreign investment and developing non-energy sectors, but effects limited.

events.title: Continued Authoritarian Rule
events.description: Turkmenistan remains one of world's most closed and authoritarian countries. Despite leadership change, basic political structure unchanged. Human rights situation remains severe, media freedom extremely limited, civil society virtually non-existent. International community continues calling for political reform and human rights improvement. Economically, country continues relying on natural gas exports, facing diversification challenges. Turkmenistan's future development depends on achieving political opening and economic modernization.
